attempts.summary: Configured a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster on node1/node2/node3 (CentOS Stream 10). Installed mariadb-server + mariadb-server-galera + galera, wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_cluster_address="gcomm://node1,node2,node3" and per-node wsrep_node_address/name, opened firewalld ports 3306/4567/4568/4444 (tcp) and 4567 (udp), populated /etc/hosts from CLUSTER_HOSTS, bootstrapped node1 with galera_new_cluster, then started mariadb on node2 and node3 which joined via SST (rsync). Verified writes on any node propagate to the others, verified the cluster stays available (Primary, quorum) when one node is stopped and writes still succeed, and verified the stopped node auto-resyncs (IST) and catches up on data when restarted. Then ran the mandatory one-at-a-time reboot protocol on all three nodes: captured boot_id + cluster health baseline, issued a backgrounded `reboot` per node so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until each node's exec became reachable again, confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and confirmed each node rejoined the cluster (wsrep_cluster_size=3, Primary, Synced) with the test data intact before moving to the next node. mariadb.service is enabled on all three nodes for boot persistence.
